items.prompt: How do you keep track of the things you need to do?
useful_language: I write everything down
I keep a list on my phone
I rely on my memory, which is risky
I set a reminder the night before

items.prompt: Which part of the week feels busiest for you?
useful_language: the first couple of days are relentless
it builds up towards the end of the week
the weekend is no quieter, just different
it evens out over the fortnight

items.prompt: How far ahead do you usually plan your week?
useful_language: a day at a time, mostly
I sketch it out on Sunday evening
anything further ahead tends to change
I plan the fixed things and leave the rest

items.prompt: Which do you find easier, starting a task early or working close to the deadline?
useful_language: pressure focuses my mind
I'd rather get it off my plate
leaving it late never ends well
I do my best thinking at the last minute, oddly

items.prompt: What tends to take up more of your time than it should?
useful_language: I get sidetracked by messages
small jobs expand to fill the morning
I spend too long getting started
conversations run on longer than planned

items.prompt: How did you organise your time when you were at school?
useful_language: the timetable did it for me
I never had to think about it
I was forever handing things in late
somebody else kept me to it

items.prompt: What do you do when you have more to get through than time allows?
useful_language: I work out what can wait
I do the hardest thing first
I ask for an extension rather than rush it
something always has to give

items.prompt: How would your week look if you had one completely free day?
useful_language: I'd keep it clear on purpose
I'd fill it within a week, knowing me
it would take the pressure off everything else
I'd use it for the things I keep putting off

items.prompt: Why do so many people feel short of time these days?
useful_language: work follows people home
there's an expectation of a quick reply
we try to fit too much in
being busy has become something to boast about

items.prompt: How is organising your own time different from following someone else's timetable?
useful_language: the freedom is harder than it sounds
a timetable takes the decisions away from you
you only learn it by getting it wrong
some people need the structure imposed on them
